_comment: Sign-off smoke test for shared Metabase report cards. After editing ANY card, run: node scripts/verify-report-live.js --manifest scripts/report-cards.manifest.json — every entry must return live, non-empty results or the edit is NOT signed off. Test the heaviest org for each card (biggest = worst case for timeouts). Add a card+org row here whenever a new shared card or large org is onboarded. org_ids come from the ORGS map in server.js; card UUIDs are the public UUIDs (SHARED_UUIDS / per-org mbUuid). TIMEOUTS: the default 60s is a tripwire, but the APP's real budget is 60s then a 120s retry (see FIRST_TIMEOUT/RETRY_TIMEOUT in server.js), so a card between those two still serves live data. Rows carrying an explicit timeout of 120 are pinned to the app's true ceiling, with the measurement in the label — a failure there means the card has passed what the app itself can survive, not that it was slow once. Do NOT raise a timeout without recording the measured number and the date.

checks.label: checkins / apex (biggest — 22,880 rows for Aug 1-23 in 22.3s, measured 2026-08-24 right after the User ID column was added; here so a lost column or a re-Texted date tag is caught rather than discovered by a blank Check-Ins tab)

checks.note: ADDED 2026-08-31 with v6. This shared card had no manifest row at all, so a dropped column or a date tag reset to Text would have surfaced as a blank Programs tab. SENDS A WINDOW: it is the only card here using {{start_date}} outside an optional block, so Metabase enforces it and the card 400s with 'missing required parameters' however healthy it is — the same false alarm the health check had on _shared/programs. 7 DAYS is what the page itself requests; this card scales badly with the range (apex 2026-08-31: 7d 1,042 rows/57.8s, 14d 81.5s, 30d 104.5s, 90d timed out past 150s). TIMEOUT 180 = the app's own ceiling (60s first try + 120s retry): it answers in ~58s alone but has been seen to blow 120s inside a full sweep, and this card has measured 7.7s-59.8s on identical inputs, so a single slow run is not evidence of breakage. V6.1 HELPED BUT DID NOT FIX THIS, and the honest numbers are below. Measured at apex 2026-09-01 over the 7-day window the page sends, AFTER the v6.1 fold and Dan's tag flip: 124.0s (1,125 rows), then a 180s TIMEOUT on the very next run. So it answers now where it did not before, but it is still past the app's own ceiling (60s first try + 120s retry) and apex will keep serving Programs from cache with live refreshes failing. NOT SIGNED OFF. Where the time is NOT: the location CTEs v6.1 removed cost 4.7s (I earlier quoted 0.88s and then 9.8s — both wrong, the second because that probe ran its own extra COUNT(*) over sessions), and `slots` costs 10.2s. Both are small fractions of ~120s, so ROLLING v6 BACK WOULD NOT FIX THIS EITHER — a conclusion worth keeping, because rollback was the obvious lever and it is the wrong one. PRIME SUSPECT is `item_tx`: a correlated LATERAL over order_item_transaction for EVERY order_item the org has ever had, unwindowed. PARKED, DO NOT OPTIMISE FURTHER (Dan, 2026-09-01): "i think the solution here is 'don't worry about it', we'll address this when we move to an api direct model. No reason to optimize something now that won't be around soon." So this row is expected to time out at apex until that move, and a TIMEOUT here is NOT actionable. The row STAYS anyway, because it still catches the things that are: a dropped column, a date tag reset to Text, an unshared card. Consequence to expect: the manifest sweep reports 21/22 rather than 22/22 for this reason alone. TELL THE TWO FAILURES APART: a TIMEOUT here is the parked perf issue and is expected; "An error occurred. (HTTP 400)" is NOT — that is the date tags reset to Text by an API push, which only a human flipping them in the Metabase UI can clear. v7/v8 2026-09-01 appended eight more columns (autopay/manual plan items and value, past due, scheduled manual, scheduled auto-pay, no-plan balance), so this row now also guards those against a silent drop.
